To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

overexpression of Erb‐2 is sufficient to cause transformation of human breast epithelial cells in vitro and that this is associated with ligand‐dependent and ligand‐in‐dependent activation of Erb‐ 2 signalling.
(1) ErbB‐ 2 over‐expression causes ligand‐independant tyrosine phosphorylaton and constitutive association of Shc and Grb2.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanisms underlying the transformation of normal mammary epithelial cells by erbB‐2, the gene product of which is a member of the epidermal growth‐factor receptor family of tyrosine kinases.
the study of the ErbB‐1, ErbB‐3, and ErbB‐4 proteins and their roles in breast cancer.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of breast tumours and the identification of novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

over‐expression of the HER‐2/neu oncogene does not cause tumorigenesis by itself but rather that it is an important factor in breast cancer tumorigenesis and that it is an essential component in the progression of breast cancer.
erbB‐2 overexpression in the mammary epithelium does not lead to mammary tumorigenesis.
the overexpression of Erb B‐2 in human breast cancer cell lines does not correlate to the presence of a specific mutation in the Erb B‐ 2 gene, but rather to a gene amplification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ErbB‐1 and ErbB‐3 were required for ErbB2‐dependent cell transformation, and that ErbB2 overexpression was sufficient to alter the ligand specificity of ErbB1 and Erb3.
ErbB‐3 is a critical component of the ErbB‐4 signalling system, and that ErbB3‐4 heterodimers are required to mediate the biological effects of heregulin on breast cancer cells.

ErbB‐1 and ErbB‐4 are the receptors for the EGF family of ligands and that the ligands for ErbB2 are the heregulins, neu differentiation factor (NDF), and the glial growth factor (GGF2) family of ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ErbB‐3 and ErbB‐4 are required for the development of mammary tumours.

ErbB‐1 and ErbB‐3 can form a complex in the absence of ligand and that this complex is sufficient to induce the formation of a Shc‐Grb2 complex, leading to the activation of the mitogenic Ras‐MAP kinase pathway.
